Hi Jun. Mara's new pay brings your take-home to ₱116,000.00 a month. After ₱76,000.00 of spending and ₱14,950.00 of minimum payments, ₱25,050.00 is left each month. ₱16,000.00 of that isn't assigned to anything yet. There's also ₱48,000.00 of 13th-month pay this December. That's a one-time amount, not monthly.

Here's how the two ideas compare. Nothing is saved until you choose.
- A: ₱10,000 a month on the card, the rest in the emergency fund. The card is paid off in 7 months, by Jul 1, 2027, with ₱9,358.80 in interest. The fund reaches its ₱210,000.00 target in 4 months instead of 10.
- B: all ₱16,000.00 on the card. The card is paid off in 4 months with ₱5,508.32 in interest. But the fund gets nothing extra, so it stays at 2.3 months of essential spending against your 3-month target.

B saves more interest and clears the card sooner. A fills your safety net much faster. I recommend A because you've chosen cash on hand over paying debt faster: it's your approved preference, and you chose that way in Sessions 1, 2 and 3.
